question: Under the Colorado CDL Manual, a driver must have a commercial driver license to drive a bus designed to seat how many persons, including the driver?
choice_a: 10 or more persons
choice_b: 15 or more persons
choice_c: 16 or more persons
choice_d: 24 or more persons
explanation: The manual states bus drivers must have a commercial driver license if they drive a vehicle designed to seat 16 or more persons, including the driver.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-59

question: To get a passenger (P) endorsement in Colorado, which sections of the CDL manual must a driver pass a knowledge test on?
choice_a: Sections 2 and 4
choice_b: Section 1 only
choice_c: Sections 3 and 6
choice_d: Sections 4 and 7
explanation: The manual states that to get the passenger endorsement, a driver must pass a knowledge test on Sections 2 and 4 of the manual, and also on Section 5 if the bus has air brakes.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-59

question: Before driving, a bus driver must confirm the bus has a fire extinguisher and which set of emergency reflectors?
choice_a: 3 reflective triangles, at least 6 fusees, or 3 liquid burning flares
choice_b: 2 flashlights and a whistle
choice_c: A single road flare only
choice_d: 4 orange traffic cones
explanation: The manual requires the bus to have the fire extinguisher and emergency reflectors required by law: 3 reflective triangles, at least 6 fusees, or 3 liquid burning flares, plus spare electrical fuses unless equipped with circuit breakers.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-59

question: Which of these must a bus driver verify are in safe working condition during the interior inspection?
choice_a: Handholds and railings, floor covering, signaling devices, and emergency exit handles
choice_b: Only the driver's radio
choice_c: Only the fuel gauge
choice_d: Only the interior lighting
explanation: The manual lists handholds and railings, floor covering, signaling devices (including a restroom emergency buzzer if present), emergency exit handles, and securely fastened seats as items that must be in safe working condition.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-59

question: What does the manual say about driving with an emergency exit door or window open?
choice_a: Never drive with an open emergency exit door or window
choice_b: It is allowed in warm weather
choice_c: It is allowed if the bus is under 16 seats
choice_d: It is allowed on short trips only
explanation: The manual states you must never drive with an open emergency exit door or window, and the 'Emergency Exit' sign must be clearly visible, with the red emergency door light (if present) working and turned on at night.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-59

question: When a driver locks an emergency roof hatch in a partly open position for fresh air, what must be kept in mind while driving?
choice_a: The bus's higher clearance
choice_b: Increased fuel economy
choice_c: Reduced stopping distance
choice_d: Nothing changes about handling
explanation: The manual warns that roof hatches should not be left open as a regular practice, and drivers must keep in mind the bus's higher clearance while driving with a hatch open.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-59

question: What does the manual say about the driver's seatbelt on a bus?
choice_a: The driver's seat should have a seat belt, and the driver should always use it
choice_b: Seat belts are optional for CDL bus drivers
choice_c: A seat belt is only required on interstate routes
choice_d: A seat belt is only required on buses over 40 feet long
explanation: The manual states the driver's seat should have a seat belt and instructs drivers to always use it for safety.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-59

question: Why must riders not be allowed to leave carry-on baggage in a doorway or aisle?
choice_a: So the driver can move freely, riders can exit by any window or door in an emergency, and riders are protected if items fall or shift
choice_b: Only to keep the bus looking tidy
choice_c: Only because it violates a local ordinance
choice_d: Only to reduce cleaning time at the end of a shift
explanation: The manual explains that baggage must be secured so it allows the driver to move freely, allows riders to exit by any window or door in an emergency, and protects riders from injury if carry-ons fall or shift.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-59

question: What does the manual say generally about hazardous materials and buses?
choice_a: Most hazardous materials cannot be carried on a bus
choice_b: All hazardous materials are allowed if properly labeled
choice_c: Buses may carry unlimited hazmat as long as it is under 500 pounds
choice_d: Only liquid hazardous materials are restricted
explanation: The manual states that most hazardous materials cannot be carried on a bus, and drivers must watch for cargo or baggage containing hazardous materials.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-59

question: How many different four-inch, diamond-shaped hazard labels does the manual describe for identifying hazardous materials?
choice_a: Nine
choice_b: Five
choice_c: Twelve
choice_d: Six
explanation: The manual states there are nine different four-inch, diamond-shaped hazard labels, and drivers should watch for these diamond-shaped labels required by the Federal Hazardous Materials Table.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-60

question: Which of the following may buses carry, according to the manual's rules on hazardous materials?
choice_a: Small-arms ammunition labeled ORM-D, emergency hospital supplies, and drugs
choice_b: Car batteries and gasoline carried by riders
choice_c: Tear gas or other irritating materials
choice_d: Labeled radioactive materials in the space occupied by people
explanation: The manual states buses may carry small-arms ammunition labeled ORM-D, emergency hospital supplies, and drugs, and small amounts of some other hazardous materials if the shipper cannot send them any other way.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-60

question: What is the maximum total amount of allowed hazardous materials a bus may carry, per the manual?
choice_a: 500 pounds total, with no more than 100 pounds of any one class
choice_b: 1,000 pounds total, with no class limit
choice_c: 250 pounds total, with no class limit
choice_d: There is no total weight limit as long as materials are labeled
explanation: The manual states buses must never carry more than 500 pounds total of allowed hazardous materials, and no more than 100 pounds of any one class.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-60

question: What is the "standee line" on a bus designed to allow standing riders?
choice_a: A two-inch line on the floor, or other means, showing riders where they cannot stand, located at the rear of the driver's seat
choice_b: A boundary marking where wheelchairs must be secured
choice_c: A line marking the location of the nearest emergency exit
choice_d: A painted line showing where carry-on baggage must be stowed
explanation: The manual states no rider may stand forward of the rear of the driver's seat, and buses designed to allow standing must have a two-inch line on the floor, or some other means, showing riders where they cannot stand.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-60

question: When arriving at a destination or intermediate stop, what should a bus driver announce, according to the manual?
choice_a: The location, reason for stopping, next departure time, and bus number
choice_b: Only the next departure time
choice_c: The current weather and traffic conditions
choice_d: The driver's name and route number only
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to announce the location, reason for stopping, next departure time, and bus number when arriving at a destination or intermediate stop, and to remind riders to take carry-ons and watch for any step-down.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-61

question: According to the manual, where may it be safest to discharge a drunk or disruptive rider?
choice_a: At the next scheduled stop or a well-lighted area where there are other people
choice_b: Immediately on the shoulder of the highway
choice_c: Only at the bus's final destination
choice_d: At the nearest unlit parking lot
explanation: The manual advises that a disruptive rider should not be discharged where it would be unsafe for them, and that it may be safer to do so at the next scheduled stop or a well-lighted area with other people around.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-61

question: What does it mean if a bus leans toward the outside while traveling on a banked curve?
choice_a: The driver is going too fast
choice_b: The bus is underloaded
choice_c: The tires need more air
choice_d: The road surface is defective
explanation: The manual warns that if a bus leans toward the outside on a banked curve, the driver is going too fast, and that with good traction the bus may roll over while with poor traction it might slide off the curve.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-61

question: How far before a railroad crossing must a bus stop, per the manual?
choice_a: Between 15 and 50 feet
choice_b: Between 5 and 10 feet
choice_c: Between 50 and 100 feet
choice_d: Exactly 25 feet
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stop their bus between 15 and 50 feet before railroad crossings, then listen and look in both directions for trains.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-61

question: How far before an unattended drawbridge (one without a signal light or traffic control attendant) must a bus stop?
choice_a: At least 50 feet
choice_b: At least 15 feet
choice_c: At least 100 feet
choice_d: At least 200 feet
explanation: The manual directs drivers to stop at least 50 feet before the draw of a drawbridge that lacks a signal light or traffic control attendant, and to confirm the draw is completely closed before crossing.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-61

question: What must a driver for an interstate carrier complete after inspecting the bus at the end of a shift?
choice_a: A written inspection report specifying the bus and listing any defect that would affect safety or result in a breakdown
choice_b: A verbal report to the next driver only
choice_c: Nothing, unless a rider files a complaint
choice_d: A photograph of the odometer reading
explanation: The manual requires interstate carrier drivers to complete a written inspection report for each bus driven, specifying the bus and listing any defect affecting safety or that could cause a breakdown; if there are no defects, the report should say so.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-61

question: What does the manual say about refueling a bus with riders on board?
choice_a: Avoid it unless absolutely necessary, and never refuel in a closed building with riders on board
choice_b: It is always prohibited under any circumstance
choice_c: It is always acceptable regardless of location
choice_d: It is only prohibited at night
explanation: The manual states drivers should avoid fueling the bus with riders on board unless absolutely necessary, and should never refuel in a closed building with riders on board.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-61

question: On urban mass transit coaches equipped with a brake-door interlock system, what happens when the rear door is open?
choice_a: The interlock applies the brakes and holds the throttle in idle position
choice_b: The interlock automatically shuts off the engine
choice_c: The interlock releases the parking brake
choice_d: The interlock disables the horn
explanation: The manual explains that the brake-door interlock applies the brakes and holds the throttle in idle position when the rear door is open, releasing when the door closes, and that this feature must not be used in place of the parking brake.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-61
